messages.subject: factor analysis
parts:
Hi,
Wondering if anyone has attempted factor analysis with INLA yet? I see one post on this forum from 3 years ago, saying it would be hard. Wondering if there are any updates since then? It would be great to have a method for factor analysis of non-Gaussian data that is not as slow as MCMC.
Thanks very much,
Chris

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] factor analysis
parts:
Hi & thanks for your email.

Factor analysis impose a fundamental problem since the model have terms
like

 .... + f_i * L_ij  + ....  

with factors f and loadings L, and both are unknown. If both are
Gaussians, then this is a case where the full conditionals are
Gaussians but the joint are far off. The way out is to move 'f' up into
the hyperparmeters, but then you do not want to many of them. also the
unidentiability of f and L makes it less straight forward. This is why
it is not added to the list of models. 

Using the new 'rgeneric' interface, you can now experiement with this
yourself; see inla.doc("rgeneric")    let me know how this goes if you
try it out.

Best
H
